 Trey Murphy III (knee) is questionable for Monday’s matchup with the Warriors. 
 Murphy III is a late addition to Monday’s injury report, which doesn’t bode well for his availability against Golden State. If Murphy III is ultimately sidelined, Saddiq Bey and Herbert Jones could absorb his minutes. 
 Trey Murphy 
 NOP 
 Forward 
 #25 
 Trey Murphy accounted for 26 points (9-of-17 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Clippers. 
 After shooting 12-of-28 from the field in his prior three appearances, Murphy made over 50 percent of his shots on Sunday. Add in the rebounds, assists and three-pointers, and this was a good finish to Week 3 for the Pelicans forward. The 26 points matched Murphy’s season high, and he’ll look to build on this effort when the Pelicans begin a four-game Week 4 on Monday against the Warriors. 
 Trey Murphy 
 NOP 
 Forward 
 #25 
 Trey Murphy (knee) finished Friday’s loss to the Timberwolves with 10 points (3-of-7 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, two steals, one block and one three-pointer. 
 Back in the Pelicans’ lineup after sitting out Wednesday’s win over the Jazz, Murphy played 34 minutes against the Timberwolves. While he did record four of his five assists in the second half, the Pelicans’ forward also attempted just one shot. Given Murphy’s importance to the team offensively, that can’t happen. Murphy’s return pushed Herb Jones (zero points, four rebounds), who had a frustrating night and fouled out in 14 minutes.

 Precious Achiuwa (leg) finished Tuesday’s loss to the Magic with 10 points (3-of-6 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, one steal and one three-pointer. 
 Achiuwa had to leave Tuesday’s game with just under eight minutes left in the third quarter with a leg contusion and did not return. His early exit gave Dylan Cardwell (1/12/1/2/2) more playing time, and he logged 29 minutes off the bench. Keegan Murray (11/2/1 with four blocks and two three-pointers) played 24 minutes as he continues to work his way back from an ankle injury.

 Zach LaVine recorded 31 points (10-of-16 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, two steals and six three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Magic.
 While fellow Kings veteran Domantas Sabonis went scoreless on Tuesday, LaVine had one of his most productive games of the season. He recorded his second 30-point game of the season, but he had to head to the locker room during the third quarter with an apparent ankle injury. Sacramento doesn’t play again until Friday, so LaVine will have a little time to recover.

 Darius Acuff Jr. amassed 29 points (10-of-21 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, six assists, two steals and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Magic.
 Acuff continues to impress for the Kings, who fell to 1-10 on Tuesday. The rookie guard has scored at least 20 points in nine of Sacramento’s 11 games, and he’s been a first-round player in 12-team leagues over the last two weeks. As long as he keeps the turnovers in check, Acuff will be a highly valuable fantasy option, regardless of league format. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Desmond Bane finished Tuesday’s win over the Kings with 15 points (5-of-19 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, four assists and four three-pointers.
 Back in the Magic lineup after missing Saturday’s loss to the Warriors, Bane had a tough night from the field. While his 4-of-13 from three wasn’t good, he was even worse inside the arc. Bane made one of his six two-point attempts, which torpedoed the overall field-goal percentage. The rebounds, assists and three-pointers were solid, however, so fantasy managers could still get some value out of Bane’s stat line. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Anthony Black amassed 26 points (10-of-17 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, five assists, four steals and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Kings.
 Black has scored in double figures in six of the seven games he’s played this season, and Tuesday’s 26 points were a new season high. With Jase Richardson replaced in the starting lineup by Jamal Cain, Black and Franz Wagner initiated even more of Orlando’s offense, and with great effect. The question now is whether Black will be made available for Wednesday’s game against the Jazz. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Player Stats

 Franz Wagner tallied 33 points (11-of-23 FGs, 10-of-10 FTs), seven rebounds, seven assists, two steals and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Kings.
 For the first time since February 8-10, 2025, Wagner has scored at least 30 points in back-to-back games. Against the Kings, he scored at least seven points in all four quarters and was perfect from the foul line. With Paolo Banchero (ankle) still out, Wagner boasts a higher fantasy ceiling and has been a top-20 player over the last two weeks, according to Basketball Monster. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Domantas Sabonis shot 0-of-2 from the field and 0-of-2 from the foul line in Tuesday’s loss to the Magic, going scoreless with two rebounds and five assists.
 To say that Sabonis had a Tuesday night to forget would be an understatement. For the first time in his career, he failed to score a point in a game in which he played at least 20 minutes. Interestingly, Sabonis didn’t take his first shot until about two minutes into the fourth quarter. Given his production so far this season, fantasy managers shouldn’t overreact to Sabonis’ showing against the Magic. That said, it will raise some eyebrows. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Isaiah Collier produced 17 points (5-of-10 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Heat.
 While Keyonte George’s ankle injury did not result in a start for Collier, his role did take on added importance. The Jazz guard had an efficient night, shooting 4-of-4 from three and committing two turnovers before fouling out. If George misses more time, Collier will be worth a look in deep leagues, even if his shooting against the Heat wasn’t his norm. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Ace Bailey 
 UTA 
 Forward 
 #19 
 Player Stats

 Ace Bailey accounted for 23 points (10-of-15 FGs), seven rebounds, two assists and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Heat.
 Bailey enjoyed one of the best offensive performances of his young NBA career on Tuesday. Shooting 66.7 percent from the field, the second-year forward finished with a season-high 23 points. After scoring at least 20 points in 16 games as a rookie, this was his first 20-point game of the 2026-27 campaign. Already without Jaren Jackson Jr., the Jazz didn’t have Lauri Markkanen on Tuesday, and those absences have raised Bailey’s short-term ceiling. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson
